newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golf-Woods makes Norman a sideshow in Sydney.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Woods makes Norman a sideshow in Sydney.

text.p: American golf sensation Tiger Woods has consigned world number one Greg Norman to an unfamiliar role as bit player at a tournament in his native Australia.

Norman, normally the focus of intense media attention every time he steps foot in his homeland, has been given second billing as 20-year-old Woods prepares for his first professional tournament overseas.
Woods drew twice as many spectators as Norman at Tuesday's pro-am before the start of the Australian Open on Thursday, according to official estimates.
Norman said he is content to surrender the spotlight to to Woods, whose hitting power has mesmerised fans and stunned the U.S. PGA tour since since he turned professional in August.
"Let him have all the attention," Norman said. "I've had it for 20 years and sometimes it's nice to step back out of it and see how someone else handles it.
"If 10,000 people want to watch him and 100 watch me, that wouldn't bother me a bit," added the 41-year-old Norman, who is chasing his fifth Australian Open title.

The potential rivalry between the world's number one and his likely heir-apparent could come into even sharper focus on Thursday when U.S. President Bill Clinton is expected to invite one of them -- or even both of them -- to join him for a round.
Clinton, a keen golfer, is making a state visit to Australia and has enough free time on his schedule on Thursday to play a few holes with either man.
On a visit to the Australian capital Canberra on Wednesday, Clinton denied reports that he had a personal golf pro in his travelling entourage.
But he added: "I'm going to need all the help I can get tomorrow." He did not say against whom he would be playing.

Clinton and Australian Prime Minister John Howard also kicked off an hour of talks by discussing the possibility of a golfing tournament pitting Australia's finest against the best players from the United States.
Woods, a three-time U.S. amateur champion, has won two tournaments in the United States as a professional and earned a reported US$60 million in endorsement deals.

Tournament organisers, who paid Woods and Norman a reported US$240,000 each in appearance money to tee up at The Australian course, are predicting an attendance of 120,000 over the tournament's four days, a third more than last year.
